classification.difficultyReason: Constructs a reciprocal graph from cosine, identifying excluded angles, asymptotes and corresponding branches.

content.prompt: On the same set of axes, sketch the graphs of $y=\cos\theta$ and $y=\sec\theta$ for $0^\circ\le\theta\le360^\circ$. The exclusions $\theta\ne90^\circ,270^\circ$ apply to $y=\sec\theta$ only.

answer.short:
The graphs meet at $(0^\circ,1)$, $(180^\circ,-1)$ and $(360^\circ,1)$. The secant graph has vertical asymptotes at $\theta=90^\circ$ and $\theta=270^\circ$.

Sketch cosine first, then take reciprocal ordinates to sketch secant. The cosine graph retains its zeros at $90^\circ$ and $270^\circ$; secant is undefined there.
answer.worked:
Sketch the cosine curve through $(0^\circ,1)$, $(90^\circ,0)$, $(180^\circ,-1)$, $(270^\circ,0)$ and $(360^\circ,1)$.

Use $\sec\theta=\dfrac{1}{\cos\theta}$. Where cosine is zero, secant is undefined, giving vertical asymptotes at $\theta=90^\circ$ and $\theta=270^\circ$.

The positive secant branches start at $(0^\circ,1)$ and end at $(360^\circ,1)$, respectively, tending to $+\infty$ beside the asymptotes. Between the asymptotes, the negative branch reaches its maximum at $(180^\circ,-1)$ and tends to $-\infty$ at both ends.

spec.description: A complete shared-axis cosine and secant graph. Dashed vertical asymptotes occur at 90 and 270 degrees. Standard accents distinguish the two series; original answer evidence uses grey curves.
spec.mathematics: Cosine is continuous on [0,360]. Secant equals 1/cos(theta), has positive outer branches and a negative middle branch, and is undefined at 90 and 270 degrees. Both curves pass through (0,1), (180,-1) and (360,1).
